notes: Built-in wall ovens only. No freestanding ranges, no countertop ovens. Each appliance subcategory is its own category build with independent spec fields, anchors, and source pools.

tier_anchors.notes: Miele: European dual-circulation convection, stainless cavity survives pyrolytic, 20-year parts, M Touch controls, lowest service callback rates. Wolf: dual VertiCross convection, Sub-Zero ecosystem, 2yr full warranty, professional standard. Both have strong professional consensus as top tier.

Thermador: BSH platform, true European convection, professional features at lower price than Miele/Wolf. Thermador Masterpiece and Professional confirmed to share same cavity, hinges, and self-clean system internally. JennAir: Whirlpool luxury line, V2 dual-fan convection, WiFi probe integration, competent but Whirlpool platform.

GE mid-luxury line. Yale first-year service rate 8.8% (surprisingly good). Café/Monogram/Profile share Selmer TN factory platform — report must disclose. True European convection on premium models. Parts availability through GE's owned national service network.

Volume brand floor for built-in wall ovens. Service ecosystem concerns carry over from dishwashers/refrigerators. LG alternative candidate (Yale 10.5% service rate). Need deep dive to confirm failure patterns — control board and self-clean damage are documented patterns in owner forums.
No calibration products. Reserved for brands with active safety recalls, no US service infrastructure, or documented structural defects.

quality.notes: True porcelain enamel (fired) and stainless steel both survive repeated pyrolytic self-clean without degradation. Painted enamel can discolor/crack. Painted steel flakes after repeated high-heat cycles. Premium brands use true porcelain or stainless; builder-grade often uses painted.

True European convection has a dedicated heating element surrounding the convection fan (separate from bake/broil elements). Fan-assisted just circulates air from standard elements. Dual-fan systems (Wolf VertiCross, Miele TwinPower, JennAir V2) provide measurably better uniformity. Standard thermal = no fan.

Hidden bake element (sealed under cavity floor) = easier cleaning, more even heat distribution. Dual hidden elements provide redundancy and faster preheat. Most premium brands use hidden; some budget models still expose elements.

Full-extension telescoping ball-bearing racks allow complete access without tipping. Wire guides require careful handling and oven mitts deep into cavity. Heavy-gauge racks that don't warp separate premium from budget.

Soft-close hydraulic hinges vs spring-loaded. Glass pane count affects insulation and exterior temperature. Quad-pane (Wolf, Miele premium) stays coolest. Double-pane budget models can exceed safe touch temperature during self-clean.
Same as all categories. Miele (+1, vertically integrated). Wolf (+1, Fitchburg WI). BSH (0, multi-factory identified). Samsung (0, multi-source). Unknown = -1.

performance.notes: Temperature delta across cavity (rack-to-rack, side-to-side). Premium ovens maintain ±5°F. Builder-grade can swing ±20-25°F. Measured by CR, Reviewed.com, CNET with multi-point thermocouples. This is the primary performance differentiator.
Time to reach 350°F from cold. Premium dual-element ovens typically 7-8 min. Budget single-element ovens 15-20 min. Meaningful for daily use.

Baking evenness score from independent testing (CR cookie test, GHI baking test). Maps to convection system design — dual-fan true European typically excellent, fan-assisted typically good, standard thermal fair to poor.

Pyrolytic self-clean at ~900°F incinerates residue completely. Some premium brands hit 950°F for faster clean. Steam-only cleans light soil but doesn't handle baked-on residue. Self-clean effectiveness is a real performance differentiator — but must balance against durability impact of repeated high-heat cycles.
Convection fan noise during operation. Premium ovens (Miele, Wolf) are notably quieter. Some budget convection fans are loud enough to be intrusive in open-floor kitchens.

True steam injection (Miele, Gaggenau) uses boiler/reservoir for precise steam. Humidity assist adds moisture but not controlled. No penalty for none — most wall ovens don't have steam and it's a differentiator, not a floor requirement.

durability.notes: Yale Appliance first-year service rates for wall ovens. Yale 2026 data: Café 8.8%, Monogram 9.3%, Miele 9.6%, Bosch 9.7%, LG 10.5%. Note: tighter spread than dishwashers/refrigerators. Whirlpool/Samsung absent (Yale premium-focused).
Full parts + labor warranty. Wolf: 2yr full. Miele: 2yr standard. Most others: 1yr. Warranty exclusion consistency rule (Rule 18) applies.
GE: owned national service network. BSH/Whirlpool: parts universally stocked. Wolf/Sub-Zero: factory-certified network (smaller but competent). Samsung: contracted network, thin real coverage.

Heating elements and control boards are the most common wall oven repairs. GE/Whirlpool: universal parts ecosystem. BSH: widely stocked. Wolf: proprietary but available (Sub-Zero parts commitment). Samsung: proprietary, availability varies.

Control board/ERC failure is the #1 non-element wall oven repair. Miele M Touch has strong reliability reputation. BSH boards have documented relay issues (same pattern as dishwashers). Samsung has documented control board pattern failures across multiple appliance categories.

Repeated pyrolytic self-clean cycles at ~900°F stress cavity enamel, door gaskets, lock mechanisms, and hidden elements. Premium cavities (true porcelain, stainless) withstand this. Some budget painted enamel cavities discolor, crack, or flake after repeated self-clean cycles. Door lock mechanism failure after self-clean is a documented pattern on several brands.

scoring_rules: Health certs report-only, no composite impact (UL 858 compliance)

BSH Platform Rule: Bosch 800, Thermador, and Gaggenau share the same wall oven platform. Thermador Masterpiece and Professional share identical cavity, hinges, and self-clean systems — differentiation is in controls and features. Report must disclose shared platform.

Wall Oven / Range Cross-Category Platform Rule: If a brand's wall oven uses the same cavity, convection system, control board, and heating elements as its range oven, this is a mandatory platform disclosure in BOTH the wall oven report AND the future range report. Deep dive findings from one category cross-validate the other.
GE Platform Rule: Monogram, Café, GE Profile, and GE standard share the Selmer, TN factory. Report must disclose which components are shared vs differentiated.
Whirlpool Platform Rule: JennAir and KitchenAid share the Whirlpool wall oven platform. Report must disclose.
Samsung/Dacor Platform Rule: Dacor wall ovens are expected Samsung-sourced (same pattern as refrigerators). Deep dive must confirm and report must disclose.
Wolf/Sub-Zero: Likely more in-house manufacturing than other brands. Deep dive should confirm. Report must disclose manufacturing location.

Yale service rate is Pool S but directional: single-region (Boston area), premium skew. Service rate spread for wall ovens is tighter (8.8-10.5%) than dishwashers (5.6-23%) — disclose in every report.
Self-clean creates a Performance vs Durability tension: high-temp pyrolytic is best for cleaning (Performance +1) but stresses components (Durability impact). Score both independently.
Score base configuration per Rule 17. Steam-enabled and non-steam variants of the same model are different products.
Score the product, not the brand (Rule 19). Single vs double wall oven = different products if internal components differ.
